questions.question: Trailers built before 1975 must have spring brakes?

options.text: Yes, they must have spring brakes.
No, they do not need spring brakes.
They are unsafe to drive.
They cannot be driven on public roads.

questions.correctAnswerText: No, they do not need spring brakes.
questions.explanation: Trailers built before 1975 do not need spring brakes. When you park a trailer without spring brakes, use wheel chocks to stop it from rolling.

questions.question: Your trailer drifts off course while backing. What should you do?

options.text: Keep backing without stopping.
Turn the top of the steering wheel toward the drift.
Turn the top of the steering wheel away from the drift.
Return the steering wheel to straight.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn the top of the steering wheel toward the drift.
questions.explanation: If your trailer drifts while backing, turn the top of the steering wheel toward the drift to fix it right away.

questions.question: When driving a bobtail tractor, you should know that:

options.text: Bobtails stop very easily.
Bobtails cannot drive as fast as tractors with trailers.
Bobtails take longer to stop than tractors with trailers.
Bobtails are illegal in most states.

questions.correctAnswerText: Bobtails take longer to stop than tractors with trailers.
questions.explanation: A bobtail is a tractor without a trailer. Bobtails need more distance to stop compared to a tractor pulling a loaded trailer.

questions.question: What is a bobtail?

options.text: A tractor without a trailer.
A tractor with two trailers.
A tractor that speeds.
A tractor that goes slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: A tractor without a trailer.
questions.explanation: A bobtail is a tractor with no trailer attached. Drivers must be careful when operating bobtail tractors.

questions.question: How should you load cargo to reduce the risk of a rollover?

options.text: Load cargo as far forward as possible.
Load cargo as far back as possible.
Load cargo as low as possible.
Stack cargo as high as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Load cargo as low as possible.
questions.explanation: To reduce rollover risk, load your cargo as close to the ground as possible. Also take curves and corners slowly.

questions.question: What does the trailer air supply control look like?

options.text: It is a square blue knob.
It is a triangular yellow knob.
It is an eight-sided red knob.
It is a round orange knob.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is an eight-sided red knob.
questions.explanation: The trailer air supply control on newer vehicles is an eight-sided red knob. It controls the tractor protection valve.

questions.question: How do you check that air reaches all trailers before driving?

options.text: Open the rear shut-off valves and listen for escaping air.
Close the rear shut-off valves and listen for escaping air.
Disconnect air supply lines and listen for escaping air.
Roll each trailer down a hill and test the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Open the rear shut-off valves and listen for escaping air.
questions.explanation: Before you drive, let air pressure build. Send air to both the emergency and service lines. Open the shut-off valves at the back of the last trailer. If air escapes from these valves, the whole vehicle has air supply.

questions.question: What is off-tracking?

options.text: When front wheels follow a different path than rear wheels.
When all wheels follow the same path.
When a load shifts during a turn.
When wheels run over a curb during a turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: When front wheels follow a different path than rear wheels.
questions.explanation: Off-tracking happens when a vehicle turns. The rear wheels follow a different path than the front wheels.

questions.question: When inspecting a coupling, what should you check under the trailer?

options.text: Detach the jaws from the kingpin.
Make sure the locking lever is in the emergency position.
Remove the safety latch.
Look into the back of the fifth wheel.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look into the back of the fifth wheel.
questions.explanation: Go under the trailer and look into the back of the fifth wheel. Make sure the jaws are clamped around the kingpin shank.

questions.question: When entering or crossing traffic in a combination vehicle, what is most important?

options.text: Sound your horn.
Make sure there is enough space for your vehicle.
Expect other drivers to make room for you.
Wait for other drivers to wave you in.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure there is enough space for your vehicle.
questions.explanation: Combination vehicles need more space than other vehicles. When entering or crossing traffic, make sure there is a large enough gap for you to do so safely.

questions.question: When a combination vehicle is lightly loaded, what happens?

options.text: It should not be driven.
The brakes do not work as well.
It will not roll over.
Most weight should be in the rear of the trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: The brakes do not work as well.
questions.explanation: When a combination vehicle is lightly loaded, the wheels may lose grip on the road. The wheels can lock up easily when you brake.

questions.question: When driving a trailer with ABS, what should you do?

options.text: Press the brakes less than you would without ABS.
Use extra braking force to make ABS work.
Brake the same way you would without ABS.
Brake less often than you would without ABS.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake the same way you would without ABS.
questions.explanation: Brake a trailer with ABS the same way you would brake a vehicle without ABS.

questions.question: When should the air supply control lever be in its "normal" position?

options.text: When changing a tire.
When using the trailer emergency brakes.
When pulling a trailer.
When using the spring brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: When pulling a trailer.
questions.explanation: The air supply control lever should be in its "normal" position when you are pulling a trailer.

questions.question: What happens when the air supply control is in the "emergency" position?

options.text: The air supply turns on.
The trailer emergency brakes are applied.
Skids are prevented.
The vehicle accelerates.

questions.correctAnswerText: The trailer emergency brakes are applied.
questions.explanation: When the air supply control is in the "emergency" position, the air supply stops and the trailer emergency brakes apply.

questions.question: What does ABS on only one axle do?

options.text: It does not change braking at all.
It is not possible.
It gives the driver better control when braking.
It puts extra strain on the other axles.

questions.correctAnswerText: It gives the driver better control when braking.
questions.explanation: ABS on even one axle gives a driver better control when braking.

questions.question: What should a driver do to prevent a rollover?

options.text: Keep cargo low.
Place cargo high.
Keep cargo loose.
Turn quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep cargo low.
questions.explanation: Keep the center of gravity low by loading cargo as close to the ground as possible. This helps prevent rollovers.

questions.question: If a trailer starts to skid, what should the driver do?

options.text: Lock the brakes.
Release the brakes.
Steer in the opposite direction.
Speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the brakes.
questions.explanation: Release the brakes so the trailer's wheels can grip the road again. Once the wheels have grip, the trailer will straighten out.

questions.question: Simply changing lanes can cause:

options.text: A whipping effect that can cause a rollover.
A trailer to straighten out.
Confusion about which lane the driver wants to use.
Other drivers to slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: A whipping effect that can cause a rollover.
questions.explanation: Changing lanes too quickly in a combination vehicle can cause a whipping effect that results in a rollover.

questions.question: If a trailer is too high, what happens?

options.text: Coupling will not be affected.
It may not couple correctly.
Coupling will be more secure.
Coupling will be easier.

questions.correctAnswerText: It may not couple correctly.
questions.explanation: The trailer must be at the right height to couple correctly. If the trailer is too high, it will not couple properly.

questions.question: After coupling, how much space should there be between the upper and lower fifth wheel?

options.text: No space
Very little space
A lot of space
Three inches of space

questions.correctAnswerText: No space
questions.explanation: After coupling, there should be no space between the upper and lower fifth wheel.
